newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo 1996 profit rises 36 pct, dividend up.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo 1996 profit rises 36 pct, dividend up.

text.p: Italy's largest banking group San Paolo di Torino said on Monday its consolidated net profit for 1996 rose 36 percent to around 600 billion lire ($361.9 million).
The bank added that it is proposing a 1996 dividend of 280 lire/share for 1996 against 240 lire/share previously.
San Paolo said in a statement that the 1996 net profit for its parent company San Paolo di Torino SpA rose 22.2 percent to 517 billion lire.

At the group consolidated level, San Paolo said its return on equity would be around 6.0 percent after 4.6 percent at the end of 1995, while the group's 1996 operating profit rose 10 percent to 2.170 trillion lire.

The bank added that the group's gross bad loans fell 5.6 percent to 7.150 trillion lire, while net bad loans also slipped to 6.4 percent to 4.170 trillion lire. The ratio of net bad loans to total loans was 3.1 percent at the consolidated level.
At the parent company level, San Paolo's 1996 net interest income rose 2.5 percent to 3.884 trillion lire, while operating income increased 9.9 percent to 5.981 trillion lire.
Operating profits at the SpA level rose 40 percent to 703 billion lire, while parent company 1996 pretax profits were up 39.7 percent at 777 billion lire.
Total bank deposits rose 6.7 percent to above 254 trillion lire, while total loans increased 4.8 percent to 99.177 trillion lire.
